To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relationship between mentors and proteges is a function of the power of the mentor and the protege and the diversity between the mentor and protege.

(1) diversified mentoring relationships have positive consequences for the mentor, mentee and organization and (2) the positive consequences associated with diversified mentoring relationships are more pronounced when the mentor and mentee are from the same ethnic group and when the mentor is a member of an ethnic majority.
diversified mentoring relationships are associated with higher levels of organizational commitment and job satisfaction, but not with lower levels of turnover intention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how power and status differences between mentors and proteges influence the nature of mentoring relationships.
the relationship between diversity, mentoring relationships, and power in work organizations.
how the power structure within organizations affects the development of mentorships and other work relationships.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diversified mentoring relationships are more likely to be beneficial to both the mentor and the protégé.

the power perspective provides an effective framework for examining the link between diversity and mentoring relationships in organizations and that the concept of diversified mentoring relationships is useful for exploring the dynamics of power and status in work organizations.
the relationship between power and mentoring is complex and multidimensional.

the more power the mentor has over the protégé, the more likely that the relationship will be homogeneous.
the more diverse a relationship is the more power is shared in the relationship.

diversity is not always good for organizations.
